title: Self-investigations by RCMP to be reviewed; Complaints commissioner finds no fault in RCMP in-custody shooting of B.C. man
article: An RCMP watchdog has launched a Canada-wide review of all cases where Mounties investigated their own officers in cases of serious injury or death since 2002.

Paul Kennedy, the chairman of the Commission for Public Complaints Against the RCMP, made the announcement Thursday while finding no fault against the RCMP in the shooting death of Ian Bush, who died while in police custody in July 2005.

The 22-year-old mill worker was arrested with an open beer outside a hockey game after giving RCMP Const. Paul Koester a false name. Bush died from a single gunshot wound to the head after the two struggled in an RCMP interview room in Houston, B.C.
Bush's mother, Linda, spoke to reporters Thursday after the commissioner's final report was released.

"People talk about closure. I don't understand closure. We've lost Ian forever and we can't change it," she said. "At home people thought we were going to get justice for Ian. ... We quickly realized there's no justice for Ian. And all we can hope to do is change how it works in the future."
Bush said she still has faith in individual officers, but doesn't have faith in the top-down RCMP system.
Kennedy said he plans to dig further into cop-on-cop investigations between April 1, 2002, and March 31, 2007, where a person was seriously injured or killed anywhere in Canada.

Kennedy released his final report into the Bush death with nine recommendations, which include installing automated closed-circuit TVs in every RCMP detachment where prisoners are dealt with and released.
He also called for every detachment to have a secure cellblock area for handling prisoners. By law, Kennedy's recommendations are not binding on the RCMP.
The review falls short of what some had hoped would be a recommendation to bring more civilian oversight of cases involving the RCMP.

Despite widespread public opinion to the contrary, Kennedy found the RCMP should continue to investigate members of the force in homicide cases rather than create an independent unit for such a purpose.
He also concluded the RCMP's northern B.C. major crime unit "conducted a highly professional investigation into Mr. Bush's death and exemplified the best practices for major crime investigations."
The New Democrat MP for Skeena-Bulkley Valley, Nathan Cullen, called the findings "disappointing."
"I attended days at the inquiry. Having seen the testimony and watched what came forward, it's very difficult to believe entirely the officer's story," he said.
